layers.title: Vegetation classes (co-produced)
layers.source: Cooley et al. (2021) vegetation typology dataset v4 (Feb 2022), CaltechDATA; classes co-produced with local experts in Ucayali
layers.licence: CC0 (as stated on the CaltechDATA record)
layers.citation: Cooley, S., Pinto, N., Aguilar-Amuchastegui, N., Vela Alvarado, J. & Fahlen, J. (2021). Vegetation typology classification and data set in Ucayali, Peru (v4.0). CaltechDATA. doi:10.22002/D1.2318. Described in Cooley et al. (2024), Ecology and Evolution 14:e70116, doi:10.1002/ece3.70116
layers.caveats: Counts and areas are this app's analysis of the CC0 polygon file. The published dataset has no oil-palm or cacao polygons; the paper's results for those classes cannot be reproduced from it. The file's 'Bosque_secudario_o_degradado' spelling is normalised here (original kept in COBERTURA_RAW).

layers.title: Terrain
layers.source: 30 m DEM, department extent (inputs/dem_ucayali_basin_extent.tif; provenance to confirm - see the data report)
layers.caveats: Terrain beyond the department extent is synthetic padding for display; elevations are neither shown nor queryable there.

layers.title: Satellite imagery (Sentinel-2)
layers.source: Sentinel-2 L2A mosaic 2025, 30 m (Earth Engine export; script in prep/)
layers.licence: Copernicus Sentinel data: free use with attribution

layers.title: Ucayali department
layers.licence: Peruvian government boundary data; the same boundaries on datosabiertos.gob.pe (publisher IGN) carry the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By)
layers.citation: INEI / IGN via the Plataforma Nacional de Datos Abiertos (datosabiertos.gob.pe)
layers.caveats: Boundaries are referential (1:100,000), not an official delimitation.

layers.title: Provinces & districts
layers.source: IGN 'Limites Departamentales' dataset (DISTRITOS_LIMITES.zip), datosabiertos.gob.pe; provinces dissolved from districts
layers.licence: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By), as stated on the dataset page
layers.citation: Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN), Plataforma Nacional de Datos Abiertos
layers.caveats: Referential boundaries at 1:100,000; simplified ~90 m for display.

layers.title: Protected areas (ANP & ACR)
layers.source: SERNANP public map service (geoservicios.sernanp.gob.pe, peru_sernanp_0102: ANP definitivas + ACR), clipped to Ucayali and simplified ~90 m
layers.period: fetched 2026-11-04 (creation year per area in the popup)
layers.licence: SERNANP viewer terms: information 'de dominio público'; derived maps authorised with SERNANP cited as source; no commercialisation; redistribution of the original information not authorised (this file is a clipped, simplified derivative; verbatim terms in the data report)
layers.citation: SERNANP - Servicio Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas por el Estado (geo.sernanp.gob.pe)
layers.caveats: Boundaries simplified for display; legal areas (ha) are the service's anp_suleg/acr_suleg values, not recomputed.

layers.title: Active fires (VIIRS)
layers.source: NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active fires (S-NPP), yearly Peru archives, bbox clip
layers.units: detections per km² per year (~1 km cells)
layers.licence: NASA FIRMS data are freely available; cite NASA FIRMS
layers.citation: NASA FIRMS: VIIRS 375 m active fire product (VNP14IMGT). firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov
layers.caveats: Detections, not burned area: small/short fires can be missed under cloud; confidence nominal/high only.

layers.title: Canopy height (ETH 2020)
layers.source: ETH Global Canopy Height 2020, 10 m (GEDI + Sentinel-2 deep-learning fusion), six 3-degree tiles mosaicked and clipped to the department
layers.citation: Lang, N., Jetz, W., Schindler, K. & Wegner, J.D. (2023). A high-resolution canopy height model of the Earth. Nature Ecology & Evolution 7:1778-1789. doi:10.1038/s41559-023-02206-6. Data: doi:10.3929/ethz-b-000609802
layers.caveats: Model estimate, not a measurement: tall-canopy heights saturate and the map carries the model's uncertainty (a per-pixel SD layer exists upstream). Display tiles are averaged to ~38 m at z12; clicks read the 10 m raster.

layers.title: Forest & loss (GEOBOSQUES)
layers.source: GEOBOSQUES (MINAM PNCBMCC + SERFOR/MIDAGRI) Bosque Húmedo Amazónico monitoring, 30 m, national rasters clipped to the department; downloaded manually (the site blocks scripted access)
layers.licence: the product metadata's LICENCIA field is '-' (no licence stated); citation required as given by GEOBOSQUES
layers.citation: MINAM (PNCBMCC) y MIDAGRI (SERFOR). 'Mapa del Bosque Húmedo Amazónico Peruano, 2000-2024'. Acceso a través de GEOBOSQUES, geobosques.minam.gob.pe
layers.caveats: Covers the Bosque Húmedo Amazónico monitoring area only ('No Monitoreado' elsewhere). Loss includes natural losses, not only deforestation; river-channel migration losses are excluded (metadata PRECAUCIONES). 2001-2016 follow the UMD methodology, 2017+ the PNCBMCC methodology. Areas are this app's analysis.

layers.title: Precipitation (CHIRPS v3)
layers.source: CHIRPS v3.0 daily (RNL, ERA5-disaggregated), 0.05 deg, via the aaguilar90 Hugging Face zarr mirror of UCSB CHC data
layers.caveats: The latest 2-3 CHIRPS months are provisional and may be revised.
layers.citation: Funk et al. (2015), Scientific Data 2:150066; CHIRPS v3.0, UCSB Climate Hazards Center

layers.title: Temperature (CHIRTS-ERA5)
layers.source: CHIRTS-ERA5 daily Tmax/Tmin, 0.05 deg; Tmean = (Tmax+Tmin)/2; via the aaguilar90 Hugging Face zarr mirror of UCSB CHC data
layers.citation: Funk et al. (2019), J. Climate 32:5639-5658; CHIRTS-ERA5, UCSB CHC

layers.title: Drought index (SPI-3)

palette.value: BrBG diverging, centred 0, fixed -3..3 (values clipped to +-3)

layers.source: SPI-3 computed from CHIRPS v3.0 monthly totals (gamma fit, Thom 1958; zero-rain mixed distribution), calibration 1991-2020
layers.caveats: The latest 2-3 CHIRPS months are provisional; class names follow WMO (2012).
layers.citation: McKee, Doesken & Kleist (1993), 8th Conf. Applied Climatology; classes: WMO (2012), SPI User Guide, WMO-No. 1090; Funk et al. (2015), Sci. Data 2:150066

layers.title: GEDI canopy height (RH95)
layers.source: NASA GEDI L2A (GEDI02_A v002), full-power beams; the paper's filters (Cooley et al. 2024, sect. 2.4) plus quality_flag = 1 and degrade_flag = 0 (this app's strict set)
layers.period: 2019-04-20 to 2025-07-09 (no shots April 2023 - April 2024: GEDI hibernation)
layers.units: RH95: height above the ground at which 95 % of the returned energy is reached, m
layers.licence: NASA Earth science data: free and open; cite the product DOI
layers.citation: Dubayah, R., Hofton, M., Blair, J., Armston, J., Tang, H. & Luthcke, S. (2021). GEDI L2A Elevation and Height Metrics Data Global Footprint Level V002. NASA EOSDIS Land Processes DAAC. doi:10.5067/GEDI/GEDI02_A.002
layers.caveats: This app's analysis. Each dot is one 25 m footprint, located to about ±10 m. Zoomed out, a 1 km grid shows the mean RH95 of the shots in each cell; at zooms 9-10 the dots are a random sample. RH95 is GEDI's own value (no ground-return transformation, unlike the paper's Table 2a).

layers.title: Land cover (MapBiomas)
layers.source: MapBiomas Perú Collection 4 (Landsat, 30 m), national rasters clipped to Ucayali
layers.licence: CC BY 4.0 - 'Los datos de MapBiomas son de uso público, abierto y gratuito, sujetos a citación' (site footer)
layers.citation: MapBiomas Perú Collection 4 (peru.mapbiomas.org). Official class palette.
layers.caveats: Oil palm is its own class (35, Palma aceitera); cacao and other specific crops have no class and fall inside 'Mosaico agropecuario' (21) - relevant when relating classes to Cooley et al. (2024). Class areas are this app's analysis.

layers.title: Burned area (MapBiomas)
layers.source: MapBiomas Perú Fuego Collection 2 annual burned area (GEE export), 30 m, department clip
layers.units: burned at least once in the year; zoomed out, share of the pixel's area that burned
layers.licence: CC BY 4.0 (MapBiomas: public, open and free use, subject to citation)
layers.caveats: Landsat-based: misses small or low-severity burns. Zoomed out, each pixel shows the share of its area that burned; from zoom 12 each 30 m cell is shown as burned or not. Burned km² per year is this app's analysis.
